operationLog.dialog.title: Operation log

@operationLog.dialog.title.description: Title of the Operation log dialog, which lists recent file operations (copy, move, delete, rename). Sentence case.

@operationLog.dialog.loading.description: Shown while the Operation log dialog loads the list of operations, or while one operation's items load.
@operationLog.dialog.loading.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.dialog.loadError: Couldn’t load your operation history. Try again in a moment.

@operationLog.dialog.loadError.description: Shown in the Operation log dialog when the history couldn't be read. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.dialog.empty: No operations yet. Copy, move, rename, or delete something and it’ll show up here.

@operationLog.dialog.empty.description: Empty state in the Operation log dialog when nothing has been logged yet. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.dialog.recordingOff: The operation log isn’t recording, so new copies, moves, renames, and deletes don’t show up here and can’t be undone. Turn it back on in Settings to record them again.

@operationLog.dialog.recordingOff.description: Shown at the top of the Operation log dialog while the user has turned recording off (the "Record file operations" switch in Settings). It explains why the list is empty or stops at some point, and that new operations can't be undone until recording is back on. The apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.dialog.recordingOff.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with recording on. Your string is a notice at the top of this dialog, above the list, shown in every state while recording is off.

operationLog.dialog.noItems: This operation has no recorded items.

@operationLog.dialog.noItems.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, when the selected operation recorded no items at all.
@operationLog.dialog.noItems.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.dialog.loadMore.description: Button that loads the next 50 operations into the Operation log dialog.

@operationLog.dialog.rollBack.description: Button on a row of the Operation log that undoes that operation. It appears only on rows that can be reversed, next to the "Can roll back" badge, and asks for confirmation before anything happens. Match the wording of the "Roll back" button in the confirmation that follows it. Keep it short: it sits inside a list row.

@operationLog.dialog.rollBackRest.description: The main button of the Operation log when the selected operation is already PARTLY rolled back and the person hasn’t narrowed the checkboxes. Pressing it (after a confirmation) rolls back everything that still hasn’t come back, so the wording says "the rest" rather than starting over. Match the "Roll back the rest" button in the confirmation that follows it (fileOperations.rollbackConfirm.rollBackRest).

operationLog.dialog.rollBackSelected: {count, plural, one {Roll back selected ({countText})} other {Roll back selected ({countText})}}

@operationLog.dialog.rollBackSelected.description: The main button of the Operation log once the person has checked items in the selected operation’s item tree. count is how many checked items will roll back; countText is that number with the locale’s thousands separator. Pressing it asks for confirmation first. Keep it short: it’s a button.

operationLog.dialog.selectedCount: {count, plural, one {{selectedText} of {selectableText} selected} other {{selectedText} of {selectableText} selected}}

@operationLog.dialog.selectedCount.description: Beside the Operation log’s main button: how many of the items that can still roll back are checked, for example "3 of 12 selected". selectedText is the checked count, selectableText the total that can roll back, both with the locale’s thousands separator; count is the total, for the plural form.

@operationLog.dialog.close.description: Button that closes the Operation log dialog.

@operationLog.dialog.operations.description: Heading and accessible name of the Operation log’s left-hand list, which shows recent file operations (copy, move, delete, rename), newest first. Picking one shows its items on the right.

operationLog.tree.label: Items

@operationLog.tree.label.description: Accessible name of the Operation log’s item tree: the files and folders the selected operation touched, with a checkbox on each one that can be rolled back. Read by screen readers only.

@operationLog.tree.columnName.description: Column header in the Operation log’s item tree: the file or folder name.

@operationLog.tree.columnSize.description: Column header in the Operation log’s item tree: a file’s size, or how many files a folder holds.

@operationLog.tree.columnStatus.description: Column header in the Operation log’s item tree: what came of each item (rolled back, skipped, or didn’t finish). Empty for items that are still waiting.

@operationLog.tree.selectAll.description: Accessible name of the checkbox in the item tree’s header that checks or unchecks every item that can be rolled back. Read by screen readers only; the checkbox has no visible label.

@operationLog.tree.include.description: Accessible name of the checkbox on one row of the Operation log’s item tree: checked means this file or folder is part of the next rollback. name is the file or folder name. Read by screen readers only.

@operationLog.tree.comesBackWithFolder.description: Shown for an item inside a folder that was moved or trashed as one piece: the item has no checkbox of its own, because rolling back brings the whole folder back with it inside. Appears as the row’s explanation and as its greyed checkbox’s name.

@operationLog.tree.folderFiles.description: Size column of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree: how many files the operation recorded under this folder. countText is that number with the locale’s thousands separator.

@operationLog.tree.statusRemoved.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree after a rollback removed it: the copy (or the file or folder the operation created) is gone again. Siblings say "Moved back", "Renamed back", and "Tags restored" for other kinds of operations. One or two words.

@operationLog.tree.statusMovedBack.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree after a rollback moved it back where it came from (undoing a move or a move to the trash). One or two words.

@operationLog.tree.statusRenamedBack.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree after a rollback gave it its old name back. One or two words.

@operationLog.tree.statusTagsRestored.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree after a rollback gave it back the Finder color tags it had before. One or two words.

@operationLog.tree.statusSkipped.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree that was skipped, either by the operation itself or by a rollback that wasn’t sure about it. The row’s explanation says which and why. One word.

@operationLog.tree.statusUnfinished.description: Status of one item in the Operation log’s item tree that the operation never finished, so there’s nothing to roll back. Avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.rollupRolledBack: {count, plural, one {{countText} rolled back} other {{countText} rolled back}}

@operationLog.tree.rollupRolledBack.description: Status of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree: how many items under it a rollback has already undone, for example "3 rolled back". countText is that number with the locale’s thousands separator. May be followed by "2 skipped" (operationLog.tree.rollupSkipped), joined by operationLog.tree.rollupBoth.

@operationLog.tree.rollupSkipped.description: Status of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree: how many items under it a rollback skipped because it wasn’t sure about them, for example "2 skipped". countText is that number with the locale’s thousands separator. May follow "3 rolled back" (operationLog.tree.rollupRolledBack), joined by operationLog.tree.rollupBoth.

@operationLog.tree.rollupBoth.description: Status of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree when a rollback both undid and skipped items under it: joins the two counts, for example "3 rolled back, 2 skipped". rolledBack is operationLog.tree.rollupRolledBack and skipped is operationLog.tree.rollupSkipped, each already worded. Only the separator (and the order, if your language needs another) is yours: use your language’s list comma, such as "，" in Chinese.

operationLog.tree.operationSkipped: The operation skipped this one, so there’s nothing to roll back.

@operationLog.tree.operationSkipped.description: Explanation of an item the original operation skipped (it never copied, moved, or changed it), shown under the item tree when the row is under the cursor and read by screen readers. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.operationUnfinished: The operation didn’t finish this one, so there’s nothing to roll back.

@operationLog.tree.operationUnfinished.description: Explanation of an item the original operation never finished, shown under the item tree when the row is under the cursor and read by screen readers. Avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.tree.unexpandableEmpty.description: Explanation of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree that can’t be opened because it held nothing when the operation ran.

operationLog.tree.unexpandableNotRecorde: Cmdr didn’t record what’s inside this folder.

@operationLog.tree.unexpandableNotRecord.description: Explanation of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree that can’t be opened: the folder was moved or trashed as one piece and Cmdr kept no list of its contents. Rolling back still brings the whole folder back. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.unexpandableCapped: Cmdr didn’t record what’s inside this folder, because this operation held a folder of over 50,000 files.

@operationLog.tree.unexpandableCapped.description: Explanation of a folder row in the Operation log’s item tree that can’t be opened. Cmdr stops listing contents once an operation holds a folder of over 50,000 files. Careful: it speaks about the OPERATION, not this folder, which may be a small one beside the big one. Rolling back still brings the whole folder back. Keep the number as written, with your locale’s thousands separator. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.tree.otherEndFrom.description: Explanation of an item in the Operation log’s item tree that landed under a different name than it came from (for example "photo (2).jpg" after a name clash): where it came from. path is a full file path, never translated.

@operationLog.tree.otherEndTo.description: Explanation of an item in the Operation log’s item tree whose other end isn’t where you’d guess (for example a rename to a different name): where it went. path is a full file path, never translated.

@operationLog.tree.backfilling.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, while Cmdr prepares an older operation’s items for the first time. A progress bar joins it when that takes long. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.tree.backfillProgress.description: Accessible description of the progress bar in the Operation log’s item tree while Cmdr prepares an older operation’s items. doneText and totalText are counts with the locale’s thousands separator.

operationLog.tree.indexesBuilding: Cmdr is getting your history ready after an update. The items show up in a moment.

@operationLog.tree.indexesBuilding.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, on the first launch after an update while Cmdr prepares its history. It clears by itself.

operationLog.tree.indexesUnavailable: Cmdr couldn’t get your history ready this time, so these items can’t show yet. It tries again the next time you open Cmdr.

@operationLog.tree.indexesUnavailable.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, when Cmdr couldn’t prepare its history after an update (for example, the disk was full). The operation list still shows; only the items of each operation can’t be listed. Cmdr tries again by itself at its next start. Keep it calm and plain: no blame, no technical words.

operationLog.tree.operationRunning: This operation is still running. Its items show up here once it’s done.

@operationLog.tree.operationRunning.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, when the selected operation hasn’t finished yet. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.rollingBack: This operation is rolling back. Its items show up here once that’s done.

@operationLog.tree.rollingBack.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, while a rollback of the selected operation runs and Cmdr hasn’t prepared its items yet. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.unreadable: Couldn’t read this operation’s items. Pick it again to try once more.

@operationLog.tree.unreadable.description: Shown in the Operation log’s item tree, in place of the rows, when Cmdr couldn’t read the selected operation’s items. "Pick it again" means selecting the operation in the list on the left. Avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.tree.togglesCapped: That’s as many items as Cmdr can select one by one. Select a folder instead.

@operationLog.tree.togglesCapped.description: Shown under the Operation log’s item tree when the person has selected or deselected (ticked or unticked) so many individual items that Cmdr can’t keep track of one more. The last one didn’t take. Selecting or deselecting a whole folder still works. "Select" is the word the Operation log uses for its checkboxes throughout. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.route.fromTo.description: Line under the Operation log’s detail header for a copy or a move: where the items came from and where they went. from and to are folder paths, never translated.

@operationLog.route.to.description: Line under the Operation log’s detail header for a copy or a move whose items came from several places: where they went. to is a folder path, never translated.

operationLog.route.fromToTrash: {platform, select, windows {From {from} to the Recycle Bin} other {From {from} to the Trash}}

@operationLog.route.fromToTrash.description: Line under the Operation log’s detail header for a move to the trash: where the items were. from is a folder path, never translated. In each branch, name that OS’s trash the way it does: the Trash on macOS and Linux, the Recycle Bin on Windows.

@operationLog.route.from.description: Line under the Operation log’s detail header for a permanent delete: where the items were. from is a folder path, never translated.

@operationLog.route.in.description: Line under the Operation log’s detail header for a rename, a tag change, a new file or folder, or an archive change: the folder it happened in. path is a folder path, never translated.

operationLog.skipReason.unverifiablePrec: Cmdr couldn’t check this against what it recorded, so it left it alone.

@operationLog.skipReason.unverifiablePre.description: Why a rollback skipped one item, shown under the Operation log’s item tree when the row is under the cursor and read by screen readers: Cmdr had no way to confirm it was still the same file, and it never touches a file it can’t vouch for. Avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.skipReason.drift: This changed since the operation, so Cmdr left it alone.

@operationLog.skipReason.drift.description: Why a rollback skipped one item: its size or date changed after the operation, so it may hold someone’s newer work. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers.

operationLog.skipReason.restoreTargetOcc: Something else is at the original spot now, so Cmdr didn’t overwrite it.

@operationLog.skipReason.restoreTargetOc.description: Why a rollback skipped one item: putting it back would have replaced a different file sitting where it used to be. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.skipReason.dirNotEmpty: This folder has something new in it, so Cmdr kept it.

@operationLog.skipReason.dirNotEmpty.description: Why a rollback skipped one folder: removing a folder the operation created would have taken files added to it since. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers.

operationLog.skipReason.alreadyGone: This was already back the way it was.

@operationLog.skipReason.alreadyGone.description: Why a rollback had nothing to do for one item: someone already undid it by hand, so it counts as rolled back. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers.

operationLog.skipReason.vanished: This is gone from where the operation left it, so there’s nothing to put back.

@operationLog.skipReason.vanished.description: Why a rollback skipped one item: it was deleted or moved away after the operation (for example the Trash was emptied), so Cmdr can’t bring it back. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.skipReason.originalGone: The original is gone, so Cmdr kept this copy rather than delete the only one left.

@operationLog.skipReason.originalGone.description: Why undoing a copy skipped one file: the file it was copied from is gone or changed, so this copy is the only one left, and removing it would lose it for good. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers.

operationLog.skipReason.failed: Cmdr couldn’t roll this one back. Its log has the details.

@operationLog.skipReason.failed.description: Why a rollback skipped one item: something unexpected stopped it (a permission, a disk that went away). "Its log" is Cmdr’s app log. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers. Avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.skipReason.locked: This is locked so that only an administrator can remove it, so Cmdr left it.

@operationLog.skipReason.locked.description: Why undoing a copy skipped one item: it carries a system lock that only an administrator can clear. Shown under the item tree for the row under the cursor, and read by screen readers.

@operationLog.summary.canceled.description: One-line summary of an operation the person canceled partway, in the Operation log list. summary is the operation's own summary counting only what it got done (for example "Copied 30 items"); plannedText is how many items it was going to handle, formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Full example: "Copied 30 items, then canceled (1,200 planned)".
@operationLog.summary.canceled.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.summary.stopped.description: One-line summary of an operation that stopped partway because of a problem (a full disk, a missing file), in the Operation log list. summary is the operation's own summary counting only what it got done (for example "Moved 1 item"); plannedText is how many items it was going to handle, formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Avoid the word for "failed".
@operationLog.summary.stopped.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.summary.copy.description: One-line summary of a copy operation. count is the number of items copied; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

@operationLog.summary.move.description: One-line summary of a move operation. count is the number of items moved; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

@operationLog.summary.delete.description: One-line summary of a permanent-delete operation. count is the number of items deleted; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

operationLog.summary.trash: {platform, select, windows {{count, plural, one {Moved {countText} item to the Recycle Bin} other {Moved {countText} items to the Recycle Bin}}} other {{count, plural, one {Moved {countText} item to the trash} other {Moved {countText} items to the trash}}}}

@operationLog.summary.trash.description: One-line summary of a trash operation (moving items to the system trash/recycle bin). count is the number of items; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch. The screenshot shows the macOS wording.

@operationLog.summary.rename.description: One-line summary of a rename operation (one item, or a batch rename of many). count is the number of items renamed; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

@operationLog.summary.createFolder.description: One-line summary of a create-folder operation. count is the number of folders created; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

@operationLog.summary.createFile.description: One-line summary of a create-file operation. count is the number of files created; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.
@operationLog.summary.createFile.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.summary.compress.description: One-line summary of a compress operation (creating an archive). count is the number of items compressed; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.

operationLog.summary.tag: {count, plural, one {Changed the tags on {countText} item} other {Changed the tags on {countText} items}}

@operationLog.summary.tag.description: One-line summary of a change to macOS Finder color tags (setting, toggling, or clearing tags on files), in the operation log's list. count is the number of items whose tags changed; countText is that number formatted with the locale's thousands separator. Keep the {countText} placeholder in every plural branch.
@operationLog.summary.tag.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.summary.archiveEdit.description: One-line summary of editing the contents of an existing archive (adding to or changing files inside a zip).
@operationLog.summary.archiveEdit.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.summary.archiveExtract.description: One-line summary of extracting an archive's contents.
@operationLog.summary.archiveExtract.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.initiator.user.description: Shown on an operation the user started themselves (as opposed to an AI client). Provenance label.

@operationLog.initiator.aiClient.description: Shown on an operation an external AI client started over Cmdr's automation interface. Provenance label.

@operationLog.initiator.agent.description: Shown on an operation Cmdr's own AI agent started. Provenance label.

@operationLog.initiator.agentEdited.description: Provenance label shown on an operation Cmdr’s own AI agent proposed and the user changed before approving (they retyped at least one name in the review). Mixed provenance: the log must not credit the agent for a name the user chose.
@operationLog.initiator.agentEdited.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.status.queued.description: Lifecycle status of an operation that is waiting to run.
@operationLog.status.queued.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.status.running.description: Lifecycle status of an operation that is currently running.
@operationLog.status.running.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.status.finished.description: Badge in the Operation log’s detail header for an operation that ran to the end. Sits beside a second badge that says whether it can be rolled back. Short: one word if your language allows.

@operationLog.status.failed.description: Lifecycle status of an operation that stopped before completing. Avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.status.canceled.description: Lifecycle status of an operation the user canceled.

@operationLog.rollback.notRollbackable.description: Rollback status: this operation can't be reversed (for example a permanent delete). The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackable.description: Rollback status: this operation can be reversed.

@operationLog.rollback.rollingBack.description: Rollback status: a reversal of this operation is currently in progress.
@operationLog.rollback.rollingBack.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

@operationLog.rollback.rolledBack.description: Rollback status: this operation has been fully reversed.

@operationLog.rollback.partiallyRolledBa.description: Rollback status: some but not all of this operation was reversed.

operationLog.rollback.partiallyRolledBac: Cmdr rolled back what it could and left the rest as it was. Rolling back the rest takes another pass and skips anything Cmdr still isn’t sure about.

@operationLog.rollback.partiallyRolledBa.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for an operation that is partly rolled back, when Cmdr can’t count its items yet. Two jobs: tell the person what happened to their files (some came back, the rest are where the operation left them), and say what the "Roll back the rest" button does. Deliberately doesn’t promise a complete reversal: the leftovers may be files Cmdr can’t match against what it recorded, and those get skipped again. "Takes another pass" means it goes over the operation once more. Reassuring and matter-of-fact; avoid the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.rollback.interruptedNotice: {platform, select, windows {Cmdr closed before this operation finished, so it may not have recorded everything the operation did. Rolling back reaches only what it recorded.} other {Cmdr quit before this operation finished, so it may not have recorded everything the operation did. Rolling back reaches only what it recorded.}}

@operationLog.rollback.interruptedNotice.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for an operation that Cmdr (or the computer) stopped mid-way, for example in a crash, so it never finished. Two facts: Cmdr’s record of it may be incomplete, and a rollback can only undo what was recorded. Calm and factual; it isn’t the person’s fault. Avoid the words error, failed, and crash. The windows branch says Cmdr "closed", the word Windows uses when an app stops; macOS and Linux say "quit".

operationLog.rollback.partialRolledBack: {count, plural, one {{countText} item is back the way it was.} other {{countText} items are back the way they were.}}

@operationLog.rollback.partialRolledBack.description: First sentence of the notice for a partly rolled-back operation in the Operation log: how many items a rollback already undid. countText is the count with the locale’s thousands separator. It may be followed by sentences about skipped items and items still waiting; each stands on its own.

operationLog.rollback.partialHeldBack: {count, plural, one {Cmdr skipped {countText} item it wasn’t sure about.} other {Cmdr skipped {countText} items it wasn’t sure about.}}

@operationLog.rollback.partialHeldBack.description: Sentence in the notice for a partly rolled-back operation in the Operation log: how many items a rollback skipped because they changed since or something else sat in their place. countText is the count with the locale’s thousands separator. Stands on its own. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.rollback.partialWaiting: {count, plural, one {{countText} item hasn’t been rolled back yet.} other {{countText} items haven’t been rolled back yet.}}

@operationLog.rollback.partialWaiting.description: Last sentence in the notice for a partly rolled-back operation in the Operation log: how many items no rollback has touched yet, whether the person left them unchecked or a rollback was stopped before reaching them (Cmdr can’t tell which, so the sentence covers both). countText is the count with the locale’s thousands separator. Stands on its own. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).

operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotice: Rolling back deletes the selected copies. The originals stay where they are.

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotic.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for a copy that can be rolled back: what the rollback button does to the checked items in the tree below. Calm and factual.

operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotice: Rolling back deletes the selected items this operation created.

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotic.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for an operation that created things (a new file, a new folder, a compress) and can be rolled back: what the rollback button does to the checked items in the tree below.

operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotice: Rolling back moves the selected items back where they came from.

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotic.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for a move or a move to the trash that can be rolled back: what the rollback button does to the checked items in the tree below. Nothing is deleted.

operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotice: Rolling back gives the selected items their old names back.

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotic.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for a rename that can be rolled back: what the rollback button does to the checked items in the tree below.

operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotice: Rolling back gives the selected items the tags they had before.

@operationLog.rollback.rollbackableNotic.description: Shown under the Operation log’s detail header for a Finder color-tag change that can be rolled back: what the rollback button does to the checked items in the tree below.

operationLog.rollback.refusalAlreadyRoll: This one is already rolling back. Watch it in the queue.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalAlreadyRol.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back but a reversal of that same operation is already under way, started somewhere else (another window, the AI agent, or an external AI client). "The queue" is Cmdr’s operation queue window, where running operations are listed.

operationLog.rollback.refusalAlreadyRoll: This one is already back the way it was.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalAlreadyRol.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back but the operation has already been reversed, so there is nothing left to undo.
@operationLog.rollback.refusalAlreadyRol.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalIsARollback: This one undid another operation, and an undo doesn’t get undone in turn. The operation it undid is still in the log.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalIsARollbac.description: Shown in the Operation log when a Roll back request reaches an operation that was itself the rollback (undo) of an earlier operation. Cmdr never rolls back a rollback (there is no redo), so nothing happened. "The log" is the Operation log dialog this appears in, which still lists the original operation.
@operationLog.rollback.refusalIsARollbac.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalOverwrote: This operation replaced files that were already there. Cmdr doesn’t keep copies of what it replaces, so the originals can’t come back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalOverwrote.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on a copy or move that overwrote files at the destination. Cmdr deliberately keeps no backup of a replaced file, so the reversal isn’t offered. Explain the limit without sounding like something went wrong; avoid the words error and failed. Apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalOverwrote.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalPermanentDe: A permanent delete leaves nothing to put back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalPermanentD.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on a permanent delete (not a move to the trash, which Cmdr can undo). Nothing was kept, so there’s no next step to offer. Keep it short and matter-of-fact; don’t hint at a recovery that doesn’t exist. “put back” is general here (restore anything at all), so pick a verb that isn’t tied to the Trash.

operationLog.rollback.refusalArchiveOver: This archive replaced an older one with the same name. Cmdr doesn’t keep copies of what it replaces, so the older one can’t come back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalArchiveOve.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on a compress that wrote its archive over an archive already sitting at that path. "Archive" is a zip/tar/7z file. Same limit as the general overwrite case: no backup of replaced bytes. Apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalArchiveOve.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalZipEditUnsu: Cmdr can’t undo changes made inside an archive yet.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalZipEditUns.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on an edit made INSIDE an archive (adding or removing files within a zip without unpacking it). Reversing that is planned but not built, so "yet" is honest and should survive translation. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalZipEditUns.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalJournalInco: Cmdr’s record of this operation isn’t complete, so rolling it back could touch the wrong files.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalJournalInc.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back but Cmdr’s own history of what the operation did has gaps, so a reversal could act on files it shouldn’t. Cmdr refuses to protect the user’s data, which the sentence should convey without alarm; avoid the words error and failed. "Record" means Cmdr’s internal history of the operation. Apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalJournalInc.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalDirectoryMe: This move merged the folder into one that was already there. Cmdr can’t tell which files came along and which were already inside, so there’s no safe way back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalDirectoryM.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on a move that put a folder where a folder of the same name already existed, so the two were merged. Merging was the right thing to do and the sentence must NOT read as a mistake; only the undo is unavailable, because the merged folder now mixes files that arrived with files that were already inside. Avoid the words error and failed. Apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalDirectoryM.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalStagedConfl: This move ran into a name that was already taken and asked what to do about it. That answer is part of the result now, so there’s no single way back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalStagedConf.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back on a move between drives that hit a name clash at the destination and asked the user how to handle it (keep both, or skip). Because that answer changed where files ended up, a reversal has no one correct meaning. Neutral about the answer given: it isn’t a wrong choice, it’s what makes the undo ambiguous. Apostrophes are curly typographic apostrophes (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalStagedConf.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalVolumeUnava: Connect the drive this operation used, then try again.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalVolumeUnav.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back but a disk, phone, or network share the operation touched isn’t connected right now. Actionable: reconnect it and press the button again. "Drive" covers external disks and network shares alike.
@operationLog.rollback.refusalVolumeUnav.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalUnknown: This operation isn’t in your history anymore.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalUnknown.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when the user presses Roll back but Cmdr can no longer find that operation in its records, most often because the history has aged out since the list was loaded. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalUnknown.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalNothingSele: Select at least one item to roll back.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalNothingSel.description: Shown in the Operation log when the user presses Roll back with none of the operation's items checked, or when every checked item was already rolled back by the time the press arrived. Actionable: select an item (tick its checkbox) in the list and press again. "Select" is the word the Operation log uses for its checkboxes throughout.

operationLog.rollback.refusalSummaryNotB: Cmdr is still reading this operation’s items. Try again in a moment.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalSummaryNot.description: Shown in the Operation log when the user presses Roll back with some items checked while Cmdr is still preparing the list of that operation's items, so it can't yet tell which items the checks cover. Actionable: wait a moment and press again. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalSummaryNot.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalTooManyTogg: That’s more items than Cmdr can select one by one. Select a folder instead.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalTooManyTog.description: Shown in the Operation log when the user presses Roll back after checking or unchecking more than 2,000 individual items one by one. Actionable: select or deselect a whole folder instead of its items one at a time. "Select" is the word the Operation log uses for its checkboxes throughout. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).
@operationLog.rollback.refusalTooManyTog.screenshotNote: The operation log dialog, pictured here with entries in it. Your string belongs to one of its other states (loading, empty, or a load error), which render in this same dialog in place of the list.

operationLog.rollback.refusalUnexpected: Cmdr couldn’t start the rollback. Try again in a moment.

@operationLog.rollback.refusalUnexpected.description: Shown on a row of the Operation log when pressing Roll back doesn’t reach Cmdr’s backend at all, so there is no specific reason to give. Friendly and actionable; avoids the words error and failed. The apostrophe is a curly typographic apostrophe (U+2019).
